title: What Canadian salary guides say, once you read the tables

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does a full stack developer earn in Montréal compared to Calgary? The answer exists, but it's locked inside PDF salary guides that nobody wants to read line by line.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Locked in a PDF. So how do you get it out?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the idea behind Salary, a data project from the AlgoÉTS club. It takes recruitment-firm salary guides and federal wage tables and turns them into data frames you can actually compare, by job, province, region and experience level.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does the PDF side look like?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One script per guide edition. It follows the current province and region as it reads, then splits each line into a job title and three salary ranges: entry, mid and senior. The result is saved so notebooks can pick it up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Those are the Job Bank wage files, one per year from 2012 to 2022. A script lines up the columns across years, combines everything into one table, and prints the best-paid jobs for each year.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what do the numbers say?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The page reads the 2023 guide, with amounts in thousands of dollars a year. The median mid-level pay is about 76 thousand, with entry around 66 and senior around 87. The step between levels is remarkably regular: senior is about 1.3 times entry for the median job.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Technology roles lead the job families at 97.2 thousand at mid level, roughly 15 thousand above engineering and marketing. Among provinces, Alberta has the highest median mid-level pay at 85.2 thousand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does a city make a big difference for the same job?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For developers, not much. A mid-level full stack developer is at 112.4 thousand in Montréal, 120.2 in Greater Toronto, 115.1 in Greater Vancouver and 111.7 in Calgary, all within about ten percent.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's reassuring for developers. Anything else people can do with it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a small FastAPI app that serves the extracted guides as JSON, and the notebooks let you rank jobs and find the widest regional gaps. The full write-up has the charts, and it's a handy starting point if you ever need tables out of a PDF.
